summary: Graceful per-tenant rewind requested after mixed-quant profile + aggressive eviction caused intermittent 5xx and tail latency
description:
Issue summary:
Customer Acme Health (dedicated) reports intermittent 5xx errors and a large P95/P99 tail after we enabled the 'aggressive-mix' quantization profile and turned on a global prefix-cache eviction policy as part of the optimizer rollout on 2026-03-12 02:10 UTC.

Impact:
- ~8% of calls for several tenant IDs returning 5xx within a 3-hour window.
- P95 latency increased from ~120ms to ~450ms for affected tenants; P99 spikes to multiple seconds.
- Some streaming sessions abort mid-response (client sees connection reset).
- Customer-visible failures for critical workflows (document summarization and claim ingestion).

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster id: dc-7 (prod us-east)
- Model variants involved: gptj-6b-quant-aggr (default rollout), fallbacks gptj-6b-stable and redwood-chat-v1-16k
- Optimizer flags rolled out via rollout-id: r-2026-03-12-07

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Send a generation request pinned to model gptj-6b-quant-aggr with sequence length ~2k tokens.
2) Concurrently send 10-20 small single-turn requests (many tenants multiplexed).
3) After a short period (minutes) some requests receive 502/503 from the runtime, and cold-start latency spikes on the rest.

Relevant logs / excerpts (sanitized):
- runtime[2026-03-12T02:18:41Z] ERROR KVCacheEvict: race detected while evicting prefix cache for tenant t-acme-14
- quant_runtime[2026-03-12T02:18:43Z] WARN kernel-selection-failure fallback-to-generic
- serving-proxy[2026-03-12T02:19:02Z] ERROR upstream 502 model-runtime-panic pid=4128

Observed correlations and hypotheses:
- Correlated increase in 5xx with the rollout window of the aggressive-mix quant profile.
- Tail latency concentrated on requests with long context windows (> 1500 tokens).
- Hypothesis A: aggressive quant profile triggers kernel code paths not fully exercised on older GPUs in cluster dc-7 causing occasional kernel fallback and longer execution times.
- Hypothesis B: combined with global eviction, concurrent prefix eviction leads to temporary KV cache misses plus retries that push latencies into the tail and in some cases provoke runtime restarts.
- Hypothesis C: increased batch-size heuristics produced by the optimizer for some tenants causes noisy-neighbor effects on certain GPU hosts.

Temporary workarounds applied by Support (per-customer):
- Pinned affected tenant(s) to 'balanced-8bit' profile using tenant override (applied at 2026-03-12T03:05Z)
  - Command: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tenant/t-acme-14/override -d '{"optimizer_profile":"balanced-8bit"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'
- Disabled global prefix-cache-eviction for tenant using tenant config key 'cache.policy=keep' (applied 2026-03-12T03:12Z).
- Routed a subset of traffic (10%) to gptj-6b-stable variant as a controlled fallback.
These actions immediately reduced 5xx rate to ~0.8% and P95 returned toward normal for pinned traffic.

Requested from Support / Customer ask:
- Formal safe rollback plan for the aggressive quant profile that supports per-tenant 'graceful rewind' rather than global immediate rollback.
- Steps to snapshot per-tenant optimizer state and KV cache keys before performing any mass revert.
- A stepwise, low-risk traffic split and monitoring checklist so customer production is not disrupted.

Proposed rollback plan (draft):
1) Create per-tenant optimizer snapshot (runtime snapshot id) for affected tenants. (Tooling: /internal/snapshots/create)
2) Apply tenant override to pin to 'balanced-8bit' (already applied for urgent tenants).
3) Disable eviction global flag with per-tenant exception: start with affected tenants, then broaden if safe.
4) Gradual traffic split: 95% -> 50% -> 20% -> 0% over 30-minute windows with health checks (5xx < 1%, P95 within 2x baseline).
5) Monitor kernel-fallback metrics and GPU error counters; if GPU kernel failures persist, initiate node-level quarantine and roll out host firmware/kernels.
6) Once stable for 2 hours, mark rollout as rolled back and schedule a postmortem.

Required engineering actions and owners:
- SRE/Infra (owner: SRE team) to watch GPU error counters and prepare node quarantine playbook.
- Runtime team (owner: Rajiv Mendes) to check quant kernel compatibility matrix and verify fallback paths.
- Support/CS (owner: Marco Ruiz) to coordinate per-tenant snapshots and customer communication.

Next steps (short-term):
- Support to provide exact CLI commands to snapshot and revert per-tenant configs (ETA: 2 hours).
- Runtime to triage kernel-selection warnings and provide immediate mitigations (ETA: 6 hours).
- SRE to prepare a kill-switch to block rollout id r-2026-03-12-07 globally if rollback is necessary (ETA: 1 hour).

Notes:
- Customer requests that any global rollback be avoided unless absolutely necessary; they prefer per-tenant rewind.
- Customer shared a separate internal incident id ACME-INC-2026-03-12 for their tracking.
comments: 2026-03-12 03:20 - Aisha Kapoor (Support): Initial triage complete. Applied per-tenant pin to 'balanced-8bit' and disabled eviction for t-acme-14. Observed immediate reduction in 5xx. Raising to P1 and requesting runtime/SRE involvement.

2026-03-12 04:05 - Rajiv Mendes (Runtime): Noted kernel-selection-failure warnings in logs. Will run compatibility checks across GPU SKUs in dc-7 and back out aggressive quant paths for affected hosts if necessary. Looking into PR runtime#3421.

2026-03-12 04:22 - SRE Team (PagerDuty): Monitoring GPU ECC and driver logs. No immediate hardware errors, pattern suggests software/kernel fallback paths being hit. Preparing node-level quarantine script.
2026-03-13 09:10 - Customer (Acme Health - Ops): Thanks — pin helped. We'd like a playbook for per-tenant rewind we can follow with your team. Please avoid broad rollbacks unless unavoidable.

2026-03-14 07:30 - Marco Ruiz (Support): Draft rollback plan added to description and shared CLI snippets. Waiting on runtime compatibility confirmation to proceed with broader revert steps. SRE requested permission to enable kill-switch if 5xx crosses 5% again.
investigation: Initial triage points to interaction between new quant code paths and simultaneous KV cache eviction. Reproducible on long-context requests and under concurrency. Runtime warnings + proxy 502s align with restart/fallback events.
resolution: Pending - mitigations applied per-tenant (pin & eviction disable). Awaiting runtime compatibility fix and SRE confirmation for safe global rollback path.
follow_up_actions: - Runtime to produce compatibility report and proposed hotfix (target 6 hours). - Support to document per-tenant snapshot/revert commands in Confluence and share with customer. - Postmortem within 72 hours if rollback proceeds.
